# Aurora Planner delivery timeline

Timeline version 3.2 was reviewed by the launch council on 2026-05-20. It records targets and gate status; it does not itself authorize release.
Design freeze was completed on 2026-04-20. Changes after that date require a documented exception and product-owner review.
Legal review was due by 2026-05-12 and completed on 2026-05-11. The completion date is earlier than the due date; the old planning draft still shows the due date only.
Marketing review was due by 2026-05-15. The review remains open because the support contact card has not been approved for the pilot-to-public transition.
Code freeze was scheduled for 2026-05-18 and passed that evening. A code freeze means release candidates are locked except for approved fixes; it does not mean every launch gate is complete.
The public launch target remains 2026-06-01 in the planning calendar. No final public launch date has been approved because the marketing review is still open.
The date 2026-06-03 appeared in Marco Bell’s 2026-05-19 contingency proposal as a possible fallback if marketing approval missed the council’s 2026-05-28 checkpoint. The council did not approve that fallback.
A date in an early April draft labeled “pilot start” refers to 2026-04-06 and is not a public-launch milestone.
Use the status column and approval record together: a due date can be past, a target can remain visible, and a proposed fallback can exist without becoming the approved release date.
The next council checkpoint is 2026-05-28. The coordinator will bring the marketing review outcome and the remaining recurring-event test evidence to that meeting.
